title: AFOTEC Data Discoverability, Semantic Governance, and AI Readiness Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE > DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE > AIR FORCE OPERATIONAL TEST AND EVALUATION CENTER > FA7046  HQ AFOTEC A 7K
description:
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION NOTICE. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The purpose of this notice is to collect information about and identify potential sources capable of performing the effort described herein pursuant to RFO part 10, Market Research and RFO part 19, Small Business Programs. This is for planning purposes only. 

  

 Any information submitted by respondents to this Request for Information is voluntary. The Air Force does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited. Respondents should not construe this notice as a commitment by the Air Force for any purpose, and should refrain from providing proprietary information in the response. 

  

 1. INTRODUCTION: This is a preliminary step by Air Force Operational Test and Evaluation Center (AFOTEC) to explore data cataloging under AFOTEC’s digital transformation strategy. An actual requirement for these services does not exist at this time. 

  

 AFOTEC A7K at Kirtland Air Force Base seeks information in relation to a potential requirement under the working name AFOTEC Data Discoverability, Semantic Governance, and AI Readiness Minimum Viable Product (MVP). This potential requirement will support AFOTEC’s need to identify, characterize, and make discoverable the data and evidence supporting operational test and evaluation activities. 

  

 NAICS code 541519, Other Computer Related Services, size standard $34M, is believed to be the best fit for this requirement. 

  

  

 2. INSTRUCTIONS: All businesses capable of providing data cataloging services are invited to respond electronically. 

  

 Responses shall include the company name, address, Unique Entity ID, CAGE code, point of contact with email address and telephone number, and indicate business size (small business, small disadvantaged business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, economically disadvantaged woman-owned small business, woman-owned small business, HUBZone, or other-than-small) using NAICS 541519, size standard $34 Million. The Air Force reserves the right to consider a small business set-aside for any subsequent acquisition based upon responses to this notice. 

  

 Respondents should review the provided Performance Work Statement (PWS) and then provide the following information: 

  

 1.  Describe the company’s experience working with data at different security classification levels. 

 2.  Describe the company’s general experience supporting Special Access Programs (SAPs) or similarly restricted environments. Do not identify specific restricted programs, customers, missions, locations, operational details, or classified information. 

 3.  Identify the deliverables and acceptance evidence your organization would recommend for a data discoverability, governance, and readiness MVP. Address, as applicable, the following artifact categories: 

             Data/evidence inventory 

             Source and ownership register 

             Test measure-to-data source traceability matrix 

             Metadata and data dictionary 

             Semantic model or ontology 

             Data readiness assessment 

             Governance and integration gap register 

             Operational workflow demonstration 

             Remediation backlog and expansion roadmap 

             Knowledge-transfer package 

 4a.   Describe the company’s experience delivering data discoverability, metadata, semantic modeling, data cataloging, data governance, or data/AI readiness capabilities in complex operational, test, engineering, or mission environments. 

 4b.  Identify the framework or approach, assessment dimensions, evidence reviewed, stakeholders involved, outputs produced, and how findings informed follow-on actions or investment decisions. Do not provide restricted customer or program details. 

 5.  Provide examples of the company’s work involving heterogeneous data sources such as telemetry, system logs, range data, modeling and simulation outputs, documents, surveys, maintenance records, or manually collected observations. 

 6.  Describe the company’s experience working in environments where data is distributed across separate repositories, security domains, program offices, contractors, ranges, or external organizations. 

 7a.  Describe how the company might approach bounding a minimum viable product (MVP) to produce usable results without requiring an enterprise-wide data migration, new enterprise data warehouse, or full production AI capability. Identify the recommended scope, major phases, Government dependencies, principal risks, anticipated timeline, and criteria for demonstrating a usable MVP. 

 7b.  Based on company experience, describe whether and under what conditions this type of MVP would require a follow-on or sustainment effort. Briefly outline recommended follow-on options, anticipated duration, key dependencies, Government versus contractor responsibilities, and the transition artifacts needed to support Government sustainment. Distinguish essential sustainment activities from optional expansion activities. Identify likely licensing, hosting, infrastructure, data-governance, training, and Government-decision dependencies.
